newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican publisher says government out to get him.
newsitem.headline: Mexican publisher says government out to get him.

text.p: The publisher of a leading Mexican newspaper who has been charged with tax evasion accused the government on Wednesday of using any means to put him in jail.

Juan Francisco Ealy Ortiz, publisher and editor of El Universal daily, had new charges of tax evasion brought against him on Feb. 19, two days after a judge cleared him of criminal wrongdoing in failing to pay $5.4 million in back taxes.

The chief of Mexico City's oldest newspaper, who has said the government is angry at its new, more critical editorial stance, took out full page advertisements in local dailies on Wednesday accusing the government of persecuting him.

He said he was up to date on his payments under a government plan for tax debtors and there was no reason for officials to try to arrest him. "It is worrisome that when judicial tribunals rule in favour of someone that defends himself in a court of law, the Finance Ministry responds by bring fresh charges that have no objective whatever but to put him in jail, rightly or not."

El Universal also ran a front page story on Wednesday quoting opposition politicians as saying the newspaperman was the target of a government witch hunt because his newspaper had become more critical in recent years.
"This undoubtedly is a form of persecution against independent journalists," it quoted Mauro Gonzalez Luna, a congressman for the leftist Party of the Democratic Revolution, as saying.

Finance Ministry officials were not available for comment on the charges but have said in the past they were going after Ealy Ortiz only as part of a crackdown on wealthy Mexicans who avoid paying taxes.
